stories.title: Jury awards $29m to Irish man's family after plane crash
stories.summary: A Chicago jury has awarded $29 million (€25 million) in damages to the family of an Irish United Nations employee who died in a 2019 Boeing 737 MAX crash, a US court spokesperson said. The civil suit was brought against Boeing by Naoise Connolly Ryan, who is the widow of Micheál 'Mick' Ryan. Mr Ryan, a father of two, was one of the victims in the Ethiopian Airlines crash that killed all 157 people on board. The Clare native had worked during the Ebola crisis in Liberia and with Rohingya refugees.

stories.title: Thousands turn out across Ireland for solar eclipse
stories.summary: Thousands of people gathered across the country to witness a rare partial solar eclipse, which covered more than 90% of the Sun. One of the biggest gatherings was at Phoenix Park in Dublin where huge crowds came out to experience the once-in-a-generation astronomical event. Crowds cheered and clapped as the skies darkened at the moment the Moon covered the Sun. A telescope had been erected to give people a safe view of the eclipse while others brought their own homemade viewing devices fashioned from cereal boxes.

stories.title: Over half a million Irish passports issued this year
stories.summary: Holidaymakers have been urged to check their passport expiry dates to ensure travel plans go smoothly during the remainder of the busy summer season. Figures from the Department of Foreign Affairs showed over half a million Irish passports were issued in the first half of 2026. On the island of Ireland, 367,471 passports were issued in total. Over 50,000 passports were issued in the six counties of Northern Ireland, of which Antrim, on 17,986, saw the third-highest figure across all 32 counties.

stories.title: Container shipping group Maersk Q2 profit beats forecasts
stories.summary: Danish shipping group Maersk has today reported a second-quarter operating profit above expectations and raised its full-year earnings guidance for a second time this year. Maersk's profit before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) for April to June stood at $3 billion, against a median forecast of $2.12 billion in a company-provided poll of 11 analysts, up from $2.3 billion a year ago. Maersk, a bellwether for global trade given its position as the world's second-largest container shipper, in June raised its outlook on the back of strong demand, particularly in Asia, and said it expected global container market growth of around 4% this year. The shipping giant has seen rising profit from turbulence in global trade that pushed up freight rates, including the US-Iran war, which disrupted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, and Houthi attacks in the Red Sea.

stories.title: Iceland, Spain experience 'dream' full solar eclipse
stories.summary: The skies above Iceland fell into total darkness as a full solar eclipse occurred over the country's western coast. A break in the clouds allowed locals and holidaymakers to glimpse the celestial phenomenon. Live footage from the capital Reykjavik showed that, despite the overcast sky, there was a cheer from the crowd gathered in front of Hallgrimskirkja church when everything went black above them. Millions of people gathered in Iceland and northern Spain to witness Western Europe's first total solar eclipse in 27 years.

stories.title: Donegal All-Ireland winner McHugh, wife killed in crash
stories.summary: Former Donegal 1992 All-Ireland winning football star James McHugh and his wife Noreen have died following a road traffic collision which happened in Co Cavan yesterday afternoon. The Cill Chartha native, who was in his early 60s, was fatally injured in the crash which involved a car and a van on the N3 at Drummallaght, between Virginia and Cavan town. Noreen McHugh, who was a passenger in the car, was seriously injured and airlifted to Beaumont Hospital for treatment. She died in hospital this evening. The driver of the van, a man in his 50s, was taken to hospital to be treated for minor injuries.

stories.summary: James McClean took part in Derry City training on Tuesday despite reports he is on his way out of the club. Derry held an open training session as part of the Féile celebrations. McClean signed shirts and chatted to supporters in the stands during the post-training meet and greet. He had arrived at the ground at 9.58am - the last player to come for the session - and did not take any questions from a large media presence. The Republic of Ireland centurion has had a troubled return to his hometown club since signing in the off-season from Championship side Wrexham.

stories.title: Henderson out for 'a number of months' after surgery
stories.summary: Ulster and Ireland second-row Iain Henderson has been ruled out for the start of the 2026/27 season after undergoing surgery on a hip injury during the summer, the province confirmed. The 34-year-old, who has not played since being sent off in Ulster's draw with the Stormers back in May, is now expected to miss "a number of months" as he recovers from the operation. This marks the third time in Henderson's career that he received treatment for a hip problem, having previously gone under the knife in 2014 and again in 2020. The club also confirmed that Bryn Ward (shoulder), Juarno Augustus (ankle), and Jude Postlethwaite (knee) all had surgeries during the offseason.

stories.title: New Irish Writing: A Thought Without Collision by Adrian Duncan
stories.summary: We present an excerpt from A Thought Without Collision, the new novel by Adrian Duncan, author of Love Notes from a German Building Site (winner of the John McGahern Book Prize), A Sabbatical in Leipzig (shortlisted for the Kerry Novel of the Year) and The Geometer Lobachevsky. Summer, 1923. Six-year-old Catherine Carolan grows restless on her parents' farm. It's already clear that her intellect will soon outgrow the two-room schoolhouse across the fields. Summer, 1951. To ease him through his final days, Dr. Josef Alois calls for someone from his past. Enter Catherine Carolan, now an Oxford professor. A novel in two strands, A Thought without Collision is a meditation on how we construct our relationship to the world around us.

stories.summary: On Wednesday, 12 August, the moon will cover approximately 94% of the sun, causing a partial solar eclipse. It will be the deepest eclipse seen from the UK and Ireland since the total eclipse of August 1999, and the last time that such an eclipse will be seen here until 2090. A total solar eclipse will cover a narrow path of our planet, likely crossing Greenland, Iceland, northern Spain, and a small portion of Portugal. Although Ireland won't see a total eclipse, the 94% partial eclipse has been eagerly awaited by professionals in the field for decades.

stories.summary: There would have to be "significant price reduction" in the cost of a drug to treat Friedreich's Ataxia for it to be covered by the HSE, according to the National Centre for Pharmacoeconomics (NCPE). Clinical Director of the NCPE Professor Michael Barry said that the HSE would need to consider how other services would be affected if the projected cost of €160 million for the Skyclarys drug were spent. The HSE's Drugs Group decided not to recommend covering the cost of Skyclarys in the treatment of the rare neurological disease, which damages the spinal cord, peripheral nerves and part of the brain. The NCPE said the price being charged by the drug company Biogen is not cost effective.

stories.title: NI minister reveals death threat after culling of 51 cows
stories.summary: Northern Ireland's Agriculture Minister Andrew Muir has said he received a threat that he will be shot following controversy over the culling of 51 cows in Co Tyrone. The minister urged MLAs to temper their language after the committee heard a claim that the public believes that there had been a "shoot to kill" approach over the animals. The Department of Agriculture, Environment and Rural Affairs’ (Daera) Humane Slaughter Team carried out the cull of the cattle on land near Fivemiletown in June.

The 18-year old McDonald, son of former Mayo great Ciaran McDonald, was one of the stories of the inter-county season as he made a rapid adjustment to inter-county football and then helped the county deliver a sensational and unexpected All-Ireland final victory amid euphoric scenes at Croke Park. A further element to the story was the knowledge all the while that McDonald was bound for Aussie Rules, having agreed to join St Kilda once he'd completed his leaving cert, which he did during the summer. "I've always dreamed of being a professional athlete," McDonald told St Kilda's YouTube channel.

stories.summary: Lisandro Martinez has joined up with Manchester United's pre-season training camp at Carton House as the last of the players afforded an extended break following the World Cup. The return of Martinez, who played in Argentina’s loss to Spain in the World Cup final in East Rutherford, New Jersey on 19 July, means Michael Carrick has an almost-full complement of players in camp ahead of Wednesday’s friendly against Leeds at Croke Park. On Sunday, England internationals Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among nine players to return amid continuing speculation over the former’s future. After Wednesday’s match, United will head to Wroclaw, Poland for their final pre-season assignment against AC Milan and former boss Ruben Amorim.

stories.title: Carney: Irish fans will embrace 'relentless' rugby league
stories.summary: Former rugby league star Brian Carney is confident the Irish sporting public will embrace next year's historic Super League fixtures at the RDS. Warrington Wolves and Wigan Warriors will face off at the newly redeveloped Laya Arena in Dublin on Saturday 24 April 2027, with St Helens taking on Hull FC at the same venue the next day. It is not an unprecedented move. While it will be the first time Super League games have been held in this country, Warrington and Wigan previously met at Shelbourne Park back in 1934, while Wigan returned to the capital in 1995 to face Leeds in a Charity Shield fixture. Corkman Carney forged a highly distinguished career in rugby league, lining out for Hull, Wigan Warriors, Newcastle Knights (in Australia) and Warrington Wolves. He also represented Munster in rugby union, won four caps for Ireland and played international rugby sevens.

stories.title: Should you 'soft launch' a new relationship?
stories.summary: Édaein O'Connell, Freelance Journalist, joined Today with David McCullagh to discuss how to debut a new relationship on social media, and whether 'soft launching' it is the way to go. Listen back above. A new relationship brings a host of exciting milestones: first date, saying 'I love you', meeting the family and taking your first trip together. But one that has become almost more stress-inducing for some people is posting a new flame on social media for the first time. When it came time for O'Connell to reveal a new relationship on her social media, she says she opted for the 'soft launch', the practice of slowly unveiling your new partner online in "drips and drabs". You will almost certainly have seen examples of this online: a picture of a romantic dinner, with an anonymous hand just in frame, or a shot of a sunlit walk, this mysterious new partner with their back to the camera.

stories.title: Sky watchers treated to best solar eclipse in decades
stories.summary: Thousands of people gathered across the country to witness a rare partial solar eclipse, which covered more than 90% of the Sun. One of the biggest gatherings was at Phoenix Park in Dublin where huge crowds came out to experience the once-in-a-generation astronomical event. Crowds cheered and clapped as the skies darkened at the moment the Moon covered the Sun. A telescope had been erected to give people a safe view of the eclipse while others brought their own homemade viewing devices fashioned from cereal boxes.

stories.title: UK professor under investigation was NEPS guest speaker
stories.summary: A University of Cambridge professor who has made headlines over an investigation by the institution into his academic qualifications and honorary appointments was a guest speaker at the Irish National Educational Psychological Service (NEPS) conference last year. Jason Arday - who became Cambridge's youngest ever black professor in 2023 - resigned last week after admitting errors in his work, but said he had faced "an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack" and was not a "liar". The university announced a probe into claims he plagiarised parts of his PhD thesis, stating that "regardless of" Professor Arday's resignation, it would "continue to investigate the circumstances around (his) appointment and tenure". The University of Cambridge said this morning that it will investigate Prof Arday's appointment by its Faculty of Education in 2022 as well as his time there since, with Vice-Chancellor Professor Deborah Prentice calling the case an "aberration".

stories.title: UK economy unexpectedly grows by 0.3% in June
stories.summary: Britain's economy unexpectedly grew in June as companies were boosted by a respite in the surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war, the start of the men's soccer World Cup and hot weather, official data showed on Thursday. Gross domestic productrose by 0.3% from May when it was revised down to show no growth, the Office for National Statistics said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast zero growth in month-on-month terms in June. The ONS said fewer firms mentioned the conflict in Iran than in previous months, coinciding with a period of ceasefire in the conflict.

stories.title: Murray: All-Ireland winners shouldn't need to raise money
stories.summary: Galway manager Cathal Murray has implored the Camogie Association to start a fund to help contribute towards a holiday - as the GAA do - for All-Ireland camogie finalists after his side had to go around the county last year "asking people for change" to try and get together enough money to celebrate their championship success. Galway were beaten 2-14 to 0-19 by Cork in Croke Park on Sunday but won the All-Ireland final in 2025 and 2019. The GAA has a fund of €150,000 which is available to the All-Ireland senior football and hurling finalists annually to go towards a holiday at the end of the season but they same pool of money does not exist in camogie. "I think Cork and Galway have been unbelievable the last three years and they've brought camogie to a different level. Them girls, when we won the All-Ireland last year, we were out fundraising. The same when we won the All-Ireland in '19. Going around to club matches with buckets asking people for fivers, asking people for tenners, asking people for change," Murray said after the match.
